items.title: Check out a new music video for FINAL FANTASY XIV Piano Collections - Till Dawn My Tears Flow
items.summary: An official tribute to the tunes of FFXIV
items.content:
0 FINAL FANTASY XIV Piano Collections - Till Dawn My Tears Flow, an album featuring piano tributes to FFXIV, is launching in Japan Oct. 14th, 2026 and then sometime in November in North America. Today brings us a new music video for the album that let’s us enjoy the track “Promises to Keep,” and you can check it out above.

FINAL FANTASY XIV Piano Collections - Till Dawn My Tears Flow delivers a collection of FINAL FANTASY XIV’s most beloved songs, arranged for piano. It contains eight tracks, including fan-favorites Morrow’s Might & Magic, Crash in the Dark, as well as a special guest appearance from vocalist Amanda Achen on Smile and Bee My Honey. From the elegant and delicate to the dramatic and exhilarating, each piece is conveyed through the expressive beauty of the piano.

Everything We Know About Final Fantasy 14 Evercold So Far
items.summary: 8.0 is shaping up to be the biggest revamp of the MMORPG since A Realm Reborn
items.content:
We’re a little less than a month away from Final Fantasy XIV Fan Fest Tokyo which will likely contain some of the final major bits of info we’ll get on Evercold ahead of its January 2027 release. But even now, there’s still a lot we know about the expansion which is looking like the most significant update to the game and its systems since Creative Studio III literally blew up the world with A Realm Reborn 13 years ago. Here’s what we know.

Evercold will come with two new job classes and we’ve already seen the first—bastion. The bastion is a tank class wielding its signature weapon, the skyltborg. What’s that you ask? Imagine a gunblade, now make it a gunshield…that also has a blade. In the class’s brief overview trailer, you can see the skyltborg defend with giant shields, attack at range with bursts of aether fire, while also getting into melee range to dice shit up. It’s an unholy amalgamation of three different disciplines—melee dps, ranged dps, and tanking—that somehow manages to work. We haven’t had official confirmation of the second class, but we know it will feature ranged physical damage. Fan theories suggest the class involves a crossbow and PC Gamer has a neat breakdown that makes a strong case in support of that.

Perhaps the biggest draw to Final Fantasy XIV , beyond the at times legendary storytelling, is the incredible detail with which players can customize their avatar. With Evercold , the game is getting a wealth of new customization options including changing Au Ra horns, nose shadings, face paint, and custom color picking for eyes, hair, and skin tones. Additionally, customization options are also coming to animations giving players the ability to have unique looks for their teleport spell and other class-specific actions.

Evercold is really taking the theme of customization to heart because for the first time, players will be able to choose how they progress in the main story quest. Where in previous expansions unfolded linearly, Evercold will allow players to choose where they take the story next, and conversations with NPCs will reflect the choices they’ve made. In the example shared by Square Enix, a player finishes area A and has the choice of visit areas B, C, or D in any order. To make sure everything progresses smoothly no matter which choice players make, each area will automatically balance its content commensurate with player levels.

One of the biggest complaints about FFXIV of late his how samey all the classes feel. All tank, melee DPS, ranged DPS, and healer abilities feel like palette / flavor text swaps of the same four-five basic actions. It seems Square Enix have heard these gripes, revealing the new “evolved” combat system for Evercold which seeks to return a sense of individuality to the job classes by streamlining their abilities (which, in turn, helps out newer players by cutting down all the buttons and ability rotations they have to learn.) Square Enix hasn’t shared the “evolved” forms of every class yet, but there are a few out there with breakdowns of how the new abilities and combos will work. But if you’ve grown too used to the way things have always been done, FFXIV will keep the old ways in place with “reborn” mode.

Evercold will also rearrange how players spend their time to cut down on the massive grind as players level multiple job classes at the level cap. Currently, to keep up with the choco-bonses you have to complete daily quests to amass the currency you use to buy higher level gear. That system will go away in favor of a weekly system in which you choose quests you can complete on your own time that’ll award you activity points…used to buy higher level gear.

Another time sink is acquiring high level gear across multiple classes. It is tough when you play more than one job class, as each one requires a different set of gear and you gotta work for all that shit. Evercold attempts to cut through that never-ending hamster wheel by allowing players to “reflect” their gear with the highest item level (essentially the highest tier of gear you own) to their other max-level job classes. It won’t work for further gear enhancements like materia, so you still gotta work for your best-in-slot stuff, but it should still make it easier to bring your second and third job classes up to speed.

Your chocobo companion is your trusty steed. You do everything together with one big caveat, you can’t take them into dungeons with you. Evercold will change that, updating the companion system to allow chocobos as combat party members. This means, if you really hate waiting in the duty finder queue, you can run a dungeon with just one other person, your two chocobos taking up the final two slots.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Diesel Apparel and Merchandise Revealed
items.summary: Italian brand Diesel has released a new Final Fantasy XIV-themed collection of apparel and merchandise in Japan.
items.content:
A new merchandise lineup based on Square Enix’s Final Fantasy XIV has appeared courtesy of the Italian brand Diesel. The latter revealed it via its Japanese official website and social media account .

The premium brand sells a variety of items ranging from apparel to necklaces and phone cases. However, all of them cost more than ¥10,000. The most affordable ones are moulded cases for the regular and Pro versions of iPhone 17, both of which have the same price tag of ¥11,000 (~$69.80). Meanwhile, the most expensive item in this lineup is the FF-D-Barus Jacket , which costs a whopping ¥132,000 (~$837.85).

The median price of this collection is ¥23,100 (~$146.50), which falls on the T-Norm shirts with ten different back designs available. These designs are also available to view right below:

This collaboration adds yet another entry to the list of merchandise collections based on Final Fantasy XIV . In August 2026, Square Enix released the Emet Selch Earring and perfumes inspired by 21 in-game jobs. It also worked with its subsidiary Taito to bring back the Mini Lamp Quest icon magnets as arcade prizes, as well as Suntory to sell cans with sticker labels featuring the MMORPG’s characters via vending machines.

The Diesel x Final Fantasy XIV Capsule Collection merchandise is now available in Japan. The items are based on the MMORPG readily accessible worldwide on PC, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X, and Switch 2 .

items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV on Nintendo Switch 2 is the best version of the game
items.content:
I have wanted to get back into Final Fantasy XIV for quite some time. I am a massive fan of everything it offers, from the art direction to the scope of the world and adventures that are held within it. I love the way that it handles narrative within the MMO format, and the massive range of locations to visit. I really, really love the music (I went to a FFXIV symphony and everything), and just generally the very Final Fantasy design of it.

Related reading: To think that I played this for the first time way back on the PlayStation 3. My thoughts back then.

But – and it’s a big but – Final Fantasy XIV is a MMO, and MMOs do demand a time commitment, both in terms of the raw hours you plug into it, and the frequency with which you need to play. Take a big break from an MMO, and it just becomes progressively more difficult to step back into.

I tried to get back into FFXIV once when I first picked up the ROG Xbox Ally . The device handled the game just lovely, but I’m not a frequent PC player, and so at some point I put the device down, took a long break, and just… let my subscription slip again.

I am, however, a frequent Nintendo Switch 2 player. By that I mean “daily”. And so now, with the game’s little icon sitting right there on my Switch 2 home screen, I’ve been logging in for at least a little playtime every day. I’ve already made significantly more progress than I did on the ROG.

Final Fantasy XIV plays just lovely on Switch 2, to start with that important point. The console’s screen is just large enough to be able to handle the very busy interface (it’s an MMO, it’s necessary) without distracting from the core action when you want to watch the fireworks. The game’s visual engine is just now ever-so-slightly showing its age with relatively primitive character models and textures – it has been going for something like 13 years at this point – but the art direction is still as stunning as ever, and I’ve loved revisiting my favourite parts of the world from my first playthrough.

Speaking of, I have started a totally fresh character and save file (I wouldn’t even be able to track down my original avatar from a decade ago, if she still exists on servers somewhere, even if I wanted to. I can’t remember my username, password, or the email address it was attached to). I love how it’s possible to play through all the base game and early expansions with NPCs, and not rely on parties of humans for the various dungeons. If you’ve ever played a FFXIV dungeon before, you’ll know that human allies tend to… well, race through it. One of the few unpleasant memories I have from my first playthrough of Final Fantasy XIV was getting to the very final dungeon of the base game and basically missing the whole thing (and being left behind) because I was trying to follow the story. The conclusion to literally dozens of hours of play.

Now, thanks to NPCs, you can enjoy most of the many expansions and all the stories within them at your own pace. And enjoy the typically excellent music, enemy layouts and dungeon design without feeling rushed, too. I even took time to take screenshots, which is one of my favourite ways to log my adventures in this game.

There is a downside, though. Because Square Enix wants to funnel players into the later expansions where, from their perspective, all the value to the players is, they’ve taken steps to streamline the earlier parts of the game, meaning that you accumulate experience points much (much) faster, and have to do far (far) fewer quests along the way. I have been exclusively undertaking the main quest line, with no side quests, let alone grinding, and my avatar is more than twice the minimum recommended level for any given quest or boss battle.

I understand why they did this, because otherwise it would be a truly intimidating, overwhelming task for a completely new player to get up to the newer expansions, but it means that those same players don’t get to spend enough time in parts of the world to really enjoy their contribution to the whole. The major cities are fine, but you’ll fly through little town areas where previously you’d spend a gaming session or two completing all the side quests. They’re barely blips and blink-and-you’ll-miss-them moments now, which really messes with the pacing for what was previously a truly wonderfully paced game that slowly walked you from one wonder to the next.

I don’t necessarily know what the solution is there, though if it were possible, I would have appreciated the option to toggle whether I wanted the accelerating levelling on or not.

Still, that’s my only gripe. The only other minor issue is that, when it comes to the chat, the Switch’s virtual keyboard doesn’t exactly allow for the same typing speed as a proper keyboard. I don’t even know if it’s possible to connect a Bluetooth keyboard to the Switch 2, as I haven’t tried yet, but even if it were possible, that would significantly undermine the portability of the experience. Currently I haven’t been social enough in FFXIV to require the chat function much, but I can see that becoming an issue later on in the game.

Those are only minor quibbles, obviously, set against a game that is hundreds upon hundreds of hours in scope, and now in an extremely portable and accessible format. FFXIV is a hobby all by itself, and now I can embrace and indulge it in full.
